body.problem: Across the analyze, workflow, and tracker lifecycle, every reasoning operation in a given run is served by a single provider chosen once for the whole run, regardless of how much capability that particular operation actually needs. High-stakes reasoning (alternative generation and judging, contract detailing, scope-boundary audits, review, build/implement, and the define-stage framing work) and low-stakes peripheral work (issue-body and summary rendering, indexer summarisation, and narrow context probes) are treated identically, so peripheral operations consume the most capable — and most expensive and slowest — model even where a weaker one would suffice, while there is simultaneously no guarantee that the operations that genuinely require high capability cannot be quietly served by a weaker one. Operators cannot express, per operation or per repository, which work deserves top capability and which can trade capability for cost and speed, and stamping a single model on the whole artifact hides which model actually produced each output.

nonGoals.text: Reaching cheaper or alternative models through any direct cloud REST integration.
nonGoals.rationale: All model access must continue to flow through the claude/codex CLI or local Ollama; a direct REST path is explicitly forbidden by the project's no-direct-cloud-REST principle.

nonGoals.text: Adding model-selection capability to the CLI subprocess wrapper itself.
nonGoals.rationale: The wrapper already accepts a model option [[c4]]; only the role-aware routing that chooses which model is new, so no wrapper change is in scope.

nonGoals.text: Redesigning or re-sequencing the analyze, workflow, or tracker pipeline logic.
nonGoals.rationale: The Epic concerns which model serves each existing step, not the steps' behaviour or ordering.

nonGoals.text: Adaptive or runtime model selection driven by live cost telemetry or output content.
nonGoals.rationale: Selection is by declared role/step identity plus operator configuration, not by dynamic heuristics.

nonGoals.text: Applying capability differentiation to embedding generation.
nonGoals.rationale: Embeddings are local-only by architecture and outside the reasoning-role surface this Epic addresses.

assumptions.text: The claude/codex CLI wrapper already accepts a model selection, so differentiating capability per operation requires no new subprocess or transport mechanism — only routing.
Today a single provider is constructed once, run-wide, at the workflow preparation site and reused for every step of that run.
Exactly one role-based provider split already exists (the summariser), proving the pattern but leaving it un-generalised across roles.
Two additional sites hardcode the top-capability CLI provider directly, bypassing the run-wide resolution, so any role-aware routing must reach them too.
The models.analyze.* catalog is the established configuration surface these concerns attach to and can be extended without a new config domain.
A per-repository provider override already exists as a distinct precedence layer above global settings.
The legacy single-provider configuration key is left unset by the installer and, when unset, currently governs all reasoning.
No existing Epic covers provider or model resolution, cost, or capability differentiation, so this work is greenfield within the workflow domain.

constraints.text: Every model access — for any role or capability level — must resolve through the claude/codex CLI or local Ollama; no direct cloud REST provider may be introduced.

The accuracy-primary / cost-least-priority principle continues to govern the critical reasoning roles: they must retain a guaranteed minimum capability and cannot be silently reduced below it, even though peripheral roles may trade capability for cost and speed.
The legacy single-provider configuration, including the unset-default path, must remain a working fallback at the lowest precedence.
New configuration must extend the existing models.analyze.* contract rather than replace it.
Per-repository overrides must continue to take precedence over the corresponding global settings.

stories.title: Declare capability tiers and assign reasoning roles to them
stories.userValue: An operator can declare, globally and per repository, which model serves each capability tier and which tier each reasoning role belongs to, so peripheral work no longer has to consume the most capable model.

localConstraints.text: There are exactly three capability tiers — core (most capable), mid, and cheap — and the cheap tier is served locally by default.
Tier and role configuration is added to the existing analyze model configuration surface, not to a new configuration domain.

acceptanceCriteria.given: an operator has assigned a peripheral role to the cheap tier and left every other role at its default
acceptanceCriteria.then: the role is served by the cheap tier's configured model rather than the most capable one

acceptanceCriteria.given: both a per-repository override and a global override exist for the same role
acceptanceCriteria.when: that role runs inside that repository
acceptanceCriteria.then: the per-repository assignment determines the tier that serves it

acceptanceCriteria.given: no tier or role configuration is present at all
acceptanceCriteria.then: the legacy single-provider selection — including its unset-default path — governs the operation unchanged

acceptanceCriteria.given: existing analyze model configuration is already present
acceptanceCriteria.when: tier and role configuration is added alongside it
acceptanceCriteria.then: the pre-existing configuration keys continue to be honored rather than replaced

stories.title: Guarantee a minimum capability floor for critical roles
stories.userValue: Operators are assured that critical reasoning roles can never be silently served below a configured minimum capability, preserving accuracy-first for the work that genuinely needs it while still letting peripheral roles run cheaper.

localConstraints.text: A configured minimum capability applies to critical (core) roles; when none is configured, a built-in default minimum applies.

acceptanceCriteria.given: a critical role has been overridden to a model weaker than the configured minimum
acceptanceCriteria.when: that role is resolved for a run
acceptanceCriteria.then: it is served at no less than the minimum capability and the attempted downgrade does not silently take effect

acceptanceCriteria.given: no minimum capability is explicitly configured
acceptanceCriteria.then: the built-in default minimum applies to it

acceptanceCriteria.given: a peripheral (non-critical) role configured below the critical minimum
acceptanceCriteria.then: it is permitted to run at the lower capability

stories.title: Match every reasoning operation to the model its role warrants
stories.userValue: Every reasoning operation across the analyze, workflow, and tracker lifecycle is served by the model configured for its own role, instead of one provider chosen once for the whole run.

acceptanceCriteria.given: a run that contains both critical and peripheral operations
acceptanceCriteria.then: each is served by the model configured for its own role rather than by a single run-wide choice

acceptanceCriteria.given: a resolved role at any tier, including the cheap tier
acceptanceCriteria.then: the access flows through the local runtime or the claude/codex CLI and never through a direct cloud REST path

acceptanceCriteria.given: a role for which no override is configured
acceptanceCriteria.then: it falls to its tier default, then to the legacy single-provider setting, in that order of precedence

stories.title: Record the actual model that produced each output
stories.userValue: Each produced artifact records which model actually generated each of its outputs, so operators can audit where capability was spent rather than seeing one model attributed to the entire run.

localConstraints.text: Each produced output records the model that generated it, superseding the single per-run model attribution.

acceptanceCriteria.given: a run whose steps are served by different models
acceptanceCriteria.then: each output carries the identity of the model that produced it

acceptanceCriteria.given: the previous single per-run model attribution
acceptanceCriteria.then: the whole-run attribution is superseded by the per-output record

stories.title: Apply role-aware routing at every reasoning site, including the hardcoded ones
stories.userValue: Operators get consistent tiering everywhere reasoning happens — issue and summary rendering, indexer summarisation, narrow context probes, and the sites that today always use the top model — with no operation bypassing role-aware routing.

acceptanceCriteria.given: the sites that today always use the most capable model directly
acceptanceCriteria.then: they obtain their model through role-aware routing like every other operation, with no direct bypass remaining

acceptanceCriteria.given: peripheral rendering, summarisation, and narrow-probe operations at their defaults
acceptanceCriteria.then: they are served by the cheap tier's locally-served model

stories.title: Document tiering and formalize the accuracy principle
stories.userValue: Operators can learn how tiers, precedence, and the capability floor behave, and the project's accuracy-primary principle is formalized to state where it is enforced and where cost may be traded for capability.

acceptanceCriteria.then: it describes the three capability tiers, the full resolution precedence order, and the critical-role capability floor
it states that accuracy governs the critical roles — enforced by the floor — while peripheral roles may trade capability for cost and speed
